pair_selection: First 12 entries of a seeded permutation of common eligible features, paired in order; no p-based selection.
direction_rule: Keep raw encoder columns and their overlap; random controls match both column norms and their mutual cosine. No Gram-Schmidt rotation of actual codewords.
aggregation: Median L2 response over four matched sparse backgrounds; report per-background fits at primary threshold fraction as sensitivity.
fit: Original fit_superellipse and additive contour normalization. Rescale additive amplitudes to chart units 0..60 solely for the original fitter's edge exclusion; exact_geodesic=False. Also fit positive-semidefinite tilted quadratic on the same normalized contour.
gating_control: After-ReLU injection through the same linear decoder; analytic response independent of anchor. Retain rank-degenerate and poor axis-aligned fits with flags.
fine_check: First frozen pair, inactive anchors, ++ quadrant, codeword and matched random, each model; 81-point grid, same primary threshold fraction.
corruption: Independent isotropic pre-ReLU Gaussian noise, per-example fixed norm = level times median encoder-column norm; keep clean target ReLU(x) fixed. Compare natural gates, gates frozen at clean input, and post-ReLU decoder-only injection, all with identical clean output.
stopping_rule: One released checkpoint per objective, dedicated identity ReLU control, six common-eligible pairs, four sparse backgrounds and three activity states, four signs, two direction kinds; analytic calibrations, fixed fine checks, and one small Gaussian-corruption probe. No training, LLM runs, or outcome-based expansion.
interpretation: Geometry and recovery are separate measurements. Differences between two objective-trained checkpoints do not identify a causal effect of CiS. Fixed-target corruption robustness is task-specific and does not by itself establish a general error-correction mechanism.
